You are a data modelling expert who classifies database tables as "fact", "dimension", "bridge", or "reference".

You receive:
  1. The full database schema with column and FK details.
  2. Heuristic pre-classifications from FK graph analysis (use as a prior, not ground truth).
  3. Business context (industry, metrics, goals).

Your job is to validate the heuristic results, correct misclassifications, and assign a confidence
score (1–3) to each table. Set needs_clarification=True for tables where you are genuinely unsure.

Definitions:
  - FACT: Records a business event or transaction. Has a date column + measures (quantities, amounts,
    rates) + FKs to dimensions. Examples: order_details, orders, transactions, events, sessions.
  - DIMENSION: Describes a business entity. Has many descriptive text/categorical attributes. May have
    outgoing FKs to other dimensions (snowflake). Examples: customers, products, employees, categories.
  - BRIDGE: Resolves a many-to-many relationship. Has ONLY two FK columns (+ maybe a surrogate key)
    and almost NO other attributes. Examples: employee_territories, user_roles, product_tags.
  - REFERENCE: Small standalone lookup table with no FKs in or out. Examples: us_states, currencies,
    status_codes, country_codes.

Critical rules — override heuristics when these apply:
  1. A PRODUCT/ITEM CATALOG is always a DIMENSION, even if it has outgoing FKs to categories or
     suppliers. Having outgoing FKs to lookup tables = snowflake pattern, not a fact.
  2. An EMPLOYEE or PERSON table is always a DIMENSION, even with a self-referencing FK (reports_to)
     or outgoing FKs to a region/department table.
  3. A true BRIDGE has almost no columns beyond its two FK columns. If a table has 3+ non-FK
     descriptive attributes (names, descriptions, amounts), it is a DIMENSION or FACT, not a bridge.
  4. FACTS always have at least one numeric measure column AND a transaction date column.
     "Header" tables (e.g. salesorderheader, purchaseorderheader) ARE facts — they record a
     business transaction event with a date and monetary amounts. Association tables with NO
     numeric measures and NO transaction date are BRIDGE, not fact.
  5. Reference/lookup tables (e.g. us_states, region) with no transactional data are REFERENCE.

Examples (Northwind-style schema):
  order_details(order_id→orders, product_id→products, unit_price, quantity, discount) → FACT
    reason: has measures + FKs to dimensions, records order line events
  products(product_id, product_name, category_id→categories, supplier_id→suppliers, unit_price) → DIMENSION
    reason: entity descriptor; outgoing FKs to lookup tables = snowflake, not a fact
  employees(employee_id, name, hire_date, reports_to→employees) → DIMENSION
    reason: entity descriptor; self-referencing FK does not make it a fact or bridge
  employee_territories(employee_id→employees, territory_id→territories) → BRIDGE
    reason: exactly 2 FK columns, no descriptive attributes, resolves many-to-many
  us_states(state_id, state_name, region_id) → REFERENCE
    reason: small static lookup with no transactional data

Output format: keep each `reasoning` to ≤8 words.

Database schema:
  organizations(id, name, slug, description, website_url, logo_url, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  users(id, organization_id→organizations, email, username, full_name, avatar_url, bio, role, is_active, last_login_at, created_at, updated_at)
  teams(id, organization_id→organizations, name, slug, description, lead_user_id→users, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  team_members(id, team_id→teams, user_id→users, role, joined_at)
  repositories(id, organization_id→organizations, name, full_name, description, clone_url, default_branch, is_private, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  projects(id, organization_id→organizations, repository_id→repositories, name, description, status, visibility, owner_id→users, start_date, end_date, created_at, updated_at)
  project_members(id, project_id→projects, user_id→users, role, joined_at)
  milestones(id, project_id→projects, title, description, status, due_date, completed_at, created_by→users, created_at, updated_at)
  sprints(id, project_id→projects, name, goal, status, start_date, end_date, velocity, created_by→users, completed_at, created_at, updated_at)
  issue_types(id, project_id→projects, name, description, icon_url, color, is_default, created_at, updated_at)
  issue_statuses(id, project_id→projects, name, description, category, color, position, is_default, created_at, updated_at)
  issue_priorities(id, name, description, level, color, icon_url, created_at, updated_at)
  workflows(id, project_id→projects, name, description, is_default, created_at, updated_at)
  workflow_transitions(id, workflow_id→workflows, from_status_id→issue_statuses, to_status_id→issue_statuses, name, requires_comment, created_at, updated_at)
  issues(id, project_id→projects, sprint_id→sprints, milestone_id→milestones, parent_issue_id→issues, issue_type_id→issue_types, status_id→issue_statuses, priority_id→issue_priorities, title, description, sequence_number, reporter_id→users, assignee_id→users, story_points, estimated_hours, logged_hours, due_date, resolved_at, created_at, updated_at)
  labels(id, project_id→projects, name, color, description, created_at, updated_at)
  issue_labels(id, issue_id→issues, label_id→labels, created_at)
  comments(id, issue_id→issues, parent_comment_id→comments, author_id→users, body, is_edited, edited_at, created_at, updated_at)
  attachments(id, issue_id→issues, comment_id→comments, uploaded_by→users, file_name, file_size_bytes, mime_type, storage_url, created_at)
  time_logs(id, issue_id→issues, user_id→users, hours_logged, logged_date, description, created_at, updated_at)
  commits(id, repository_id→repositories, issue_id→issues, author_id→users, sha, message, author_email, author_name, committed_at, created_at)
  pull_requests(id, repository_id→repositories, issue_id→issues, author_id→users, reviewer_id→users, title, description, status, source_branch, target_branch, merge_commit_sha, merged_at, closed_at, created_at, updated_at)
  notifications(id, recipient_id→users, actor_id→users, issue_id→issues, comment_id→comments, pull_request_id→pull_requests, type, title, body, is_read, read_at, created_at)

Heuristic pre-classifications:
  organizations: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  users: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 1 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  teams: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 2 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  team_members: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 2 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  repositories: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 1 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  projects: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 3 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  project_members: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 2 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  milestones: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 2 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  sprints: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  issue_types: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 1 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  issue_statuses: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  issue_priorities: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  workflows: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 1 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  workflow_transitions: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 3 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  issues: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  labels: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 1 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  issue_labels: bridge (confidence=medium) — Only FK columns; likely many-to-many resolver.
  comments: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 3 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  attachments: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  time_logs: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  commits: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 3 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  pull_requests: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 4 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  notifications: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 5 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.

Business context: Database "project_management". Domain inferred from table/column names.
